evidence.quote: the Committee has discussed ending the reduction in the Fed's aggregate asset holdings sometime in the latter half of this year, with still-ample reserves in the system.
With so much uncertainty over the level and slope of the reserve demand curve, a degree of caution is warranted.
the Fed will maintain a larger balance sheet and reserve supply relative to the pre-crisis period, with the goal of remaining on the flat portion of the reserve demand curve.
If ever it appears that our plans for the balance sheet are running counter to the achievement of our dual-mandate objectives, we would quickly reassess our approach to the balance sheet.
I favor a return to a balance sheet with all Treasury securities, allowing our mortgage-backed securities (MBS) holdings to run to zero.

parsed.rationale: The speech focuses on balance sheet operations, signaling an earlier end to runoff, caution, and a larger-than-pre-crisis balance sheet, which leans dovish relative to continued runoff. It offers no assessment of inflation or activity, and the MBS-to-zero preference is mainly a composition point.
